_source: George Winter, How to Mix Drinks — Bar Keeper's Handbook (New York, 1884). Public domain. Vision-transcribed from the archive.org scan (howtomixdrinksba00wint) page images via IIIF — not from OCR text. Printed pages 24, 47, 48, 52.
_notes: Period measures modernized: wine-glass = 60 ml, half wine-glass = 30 ml, tablespoon = 15 ml. 'Peruvian Bitters' and 'Orinoco Bitters' mapped to Angostura aromatic bitters with notes; gum syrup to simple syrup; Italian Vermouth / 'Vermouth' to sweet vermouth; Holland gin to Genever. The book's Whiskey Cocktail is omitted: its continuation pages (49-50) are missing from the scan and a faithful transcription cannot be completed.

collection.name: Winter 1884
collection.description: From George Winter's Bar Keeper's Handbook (1884) — the bar as it stood one year before the ledger this app is dressed as. Contains an equal-parts Manhattan and the Turf Club, the Martini's immediate ancestor.

recipe.name: Gin Cocktail (1884)
recipe.instructions: Add the gum syrup, bitters, absinthe and gin to a large bar glass. Fill with fine ice; stir well; squeeze from a lemon peel on top, and serve.
recipe.description: From George Winter's Bar Keeper's Handbook (1884), p. 24. Made with Holland gin — the malty Dutch style that preceded London dry in American bars.
recipe.source: George Winter, How to Mix Drinks (1884), p. 24

recipe.name: Absinthe Cocktail (1884)
recipe.instructions: Fill a large bar glass with ice. Add the gum syrup, bitters, curaçao, water and absinthe. Stir it well with a spoon; strain into a fancy cocktail glass; squeeze lemon peel on top, then serve.
recipe.description: From George Winter's Bar Keeper's Handbook (1884), p. 24. Three-quarters of a wine glass of absinthe — the 1880s did not sip it in dashes.
recipe.source: George Winter, How to Mix Drinks (1884), p. 24

recipe.name: Turf Club Cocktail (1884)
recipe.instructions: Add the bitters, Tom gin and Italian vermouth to a glass. Fill three-quarters full of fine ice, stir well with a spoon and strain into a fancy cocktail glass, then serve.
recipe.description: From George Winter's Bar Keeper's Handbook (1884), p. 47. Equal parts Old Tom gin and Italian vermouth with bitters — the drink standing directly between the Manhattan and the Martini, printed years before the word Martini reached a book.
recipe.source: George Winter, How to Mix Drinks (1884), p. 47

ingredients.note: One-half wine glass of Tom gin

recipe.name: Sam Ward (1884)
recipe.instructions: Fill a fancy cocktail glass with fine crystal ice. Add the Chartreuse and curaçao. Stir well with a spoon. Peel the rind of a lemon the same as you would an apple, dip in sugar and place on top in tasty manner, then serve.
recipe.description: From George Winter's Bar Keeper's Handbook (1884), p. 47. Named for Samuel Ward — lobbyist, gourmet, and "King of the Lobby" — an equal-parts liqueur cocktail with a sugared lemon rind.
recipe.source: George Winter, How to Mix Drinks (1884), p. 47
recipe.garnish: Sugared lemon rind, pared in one piece

recipe.name: Golden Fizz (1884)
recipe.instructions: Add the lemon juice, sugar, Old Tom gin and egg yolk to a large bar glass. Fill the glass three-quarters full of fine ice. Shake well with shaker, strain into a fancy fizz glass, fill the balance with syphon seltzer, and serve.
recipe.description: From George Winter's Bar Keeper's Handbook (1884), p. 48. A gin fizz with the yolk only — its silver twin takes the white.
recipe.source: George Winter, How to Mix Drinks (1884), p. 48

recipe.name: Old Tom Gin Cocktail (1884)
recipe.instructions: Add the bitters, gum syrup and absinthe to a large bar glass. Fill the glass with fine shaved ice. Add the Old Tom gin; stir well with a spoon, strain into a fancy cocktail glass, twist the oil from a piece of lemon peel on top, then serve.
recipe.description: From George Winter's Bar Keeper's Handbook (1884), p. 48.
recipe.source: George Winter, How to Mix Drinks (1884), p. 48
recipe.garnish: Lemon peel, oil twisted on top

recipe.name: Manhattan Cocktail (1884)
recipe.instructions: Add the bitters, gum syrup, whiskey and vermouth to a large bar glass. Fill the glass three-quarters full of fine shaved ice, mix well with a spoon, strain into a fancy cocktail glass and serve.
recipe.description: From George Winter's Bar Keeper's Handbook (1884), p. 52 — one of the earliest printed Manhattans: equal parts whiskey and vermouth, Peruvian bitters, a touch of gum.
recipe.source: George Winter, How to Mix Drinks (1884), p. 52

ingredients.note: One-half wine glass; simply 'whiskey' in the original
Simply 'Vermouth' in the original — Italian in period

recipe.name: Gin Puff (1884)
recipe.instructions: Add the Holland gin to a large fancy bar glass. Fill the glass half full of fresh milk and the balance with syphon seltzer, then serve.
recipe.description: From George Winter's Bar Keeper's Handbook (1884), p. 52. Gin, milk and seltzer — the puff was the 1880s' idea of a light drink.
recipe.source: George Winter, How to Mix Drinks (1884), p. 52
